rows.description: Friends push me to drink or use "just to fit in" and call me boring. I feel torn. Wise: a real friend accepts a no; say it simply, leave early, and find people who like me sober.

rows.description: My parent finds out and shouts, and I feel cornered and defensive. Wise: hear the fear inside the anger, agree to a plan, and accept help. Harmful: lying or slamming doors to keep the habit.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, dependence, manipulation, obsession, shame, trust

rows.description: I finally book an appointment for my drinking or gaming problem. Nervous and relieved. Wise: honesty with a professional is the start of recovery; go back even after a slip. Harmful: presenting only the softer half of the story.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, dependence, manipulation, obsession, shame
related mind states: anxiety, relief, resentment, trust

rows.description: A support group takes me in without judgement. I feel relief and belonging. Wise: return regularly, be honest and help others later. Harmful: swapping the addiction for dependence on the group's approval only.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, dependence, manipulation, obsession, shame, trust

rows.description: Betting apps promise a quick win, and I chase losses at 2 am. Wise: block the apps, tell someone, and understand that the game is built to keep me playing. Harmful: borrowing to win back what I lost.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, dependence, manipulation, shame, trust

rows.description: My friend says she feels hopeless and I want to help. Wise: listen without judging, take it seriously, stay with her and help her reach a counsellor, doctor or helpline. Harmful: promising to keep it secret or brushing it off.
